newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - November 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - November 29.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

President Kumaratunga, on a state visit to France, tells French businessmen that Sri Lanka welcomes investment in ceramics, glass and rubber-based products, light engineering, electronics, textiles and software.
Media Minister Dharmasiri Senanayake opens country's first media training institute, and says "it is the first step towards recognising journalism as a profession."

LTTE (Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam) infiltrators in the northern Jaffna peninsula killed by the army, are described as civillians by rebel supporters and included in lists of missing persons, say security sources.
Police uncover LTTE plot to bomb Colombo's National Hospital, using women cadres disguised as nurses, police sources say.
Police arrest LTTE rebel from Colombo, who was used to hide explosives smuggled into the capital, in the eastern town of Vavunia.
Police in civilian dress to be used to catch reckless private bus drivers.
After general amnesty offered to army deserters expires on November 30, they will be arrested on sight, says Deputy Defence Minister, General Anuruddha Ratwatte.

Analysts say President Kumaratunga's recent state visit to France, during which Paris said it backed her efforts to bring peace to Sri Lanka, is a blow to LTTE, which has offices in the French capital.
